Equalizer: Audio frequency-response processor, not social equality.
Post gain: Signal level adjustment after EQ processing, in dB; permits attenuation as well as amplification. Not financial profit.
Gain: Audio signal level adjustment in dB, positive or negative. Not financial profit.
Bands: Frequency bands in an audio equalizer. Not music groups, belts or radio stations.
Selected band: Currently selected frequency band in the equalizer.
Flat: Preset with zero equalizer gain at every frequency. Not an apartment; does not imply muted audio.
Reset to flat: Restore zero gain in all EQ bands. Does not mute playback.
Balance: Left/right audio channel balance. Not bank balance or physical equilibrium.
Quit app: Exit the process and unload audio processing; closing the window alone keeps the app running.
Natural mic EQ: Microphone equalization feature intended to produce natural-sounding audio. Not a claim that the microphone has a measured neutral response.
Use system locale: Use the operating system regional number/date formatting settings; independent of interface language.
Listening preset: Saved equalizer settings for playback. Not a listening device.
Lock EQ: Prevent accidental editing of EQ controls; not encryption or a security lock.
Undo: Reverse the previous editable setting change.
Filter Q: Dimensionless quality factor controlling filter sharpness: higher Q produces a narrower peak. Not a bandwidth in Hz. Stable processing parameter remains q.
Apply amplifier correction?: Confirmation title before applying a measured amplifier frequency-response correction. Correction changes EQ, not hardware gain or firmware.
Equalizer conflict: Warning title when another equalizer or processing owner conflicts with this app. It is a software routing/ownership conflict, not clipping or a bad acoustic measurement.
Measurement conditions: %1: Label for imported amplifier measurement conditions, including electrical load and tone settings. %1 is verbatim supplied data.
Source: %1: Published measurement source URL. %1 is verbatim source data, not a translated equipment identifier.
Apply only if these conditions match you: Only apply measured amplifier EQ correction if the measurement setup matches the user’s actual equipment. This prevents using a load-dependent curve indiscriminately.
Correction filters:: Heading for the actual bounded EQ correction filters in the imported profile; JSON identifiers below remain unchanged.
Measurement: %1: Label for verbatim published speaker measurement attribution, not a new calibration run.
Peaking filter: Bell-shaped parametric EQ filter centered at its frequency; this is not a peak/clipping indicator.
Low-shelf filter: Shelving EQ: raise/lower the low-frequency region. Do not translate as low-pass; it is not a cutoff filter.
High-shelf filter: Shelving EQ: raise/lower the high-frequency region. Do not translate as high-pass; it is not a cutoff filter.
Spinorama AutoEQ: correction gain is lim: Speaker correction safety policy. %1 is the signed gain limit including dB, %2 is the dimensionless Q limit, %3 is the minimum boost frequency including Hz. Listening preset EQ is summed separately and can exceed these correction-only bounds. Spinorama AutoEQ is a name.
Bookshelf speaker: Speaker enclosure/installation category in equipment taxonomy. Display label only; original equipmentType key is preserved. Center means center-channel speaker, not a location control.
Center speaker: Speaker enclosure/installation category in equipment taxonomy. Display label only; original equipmentType key is preserved. Center means center-channel speaker, not a location control.
Floorstanding speaker: Speaker enclosure/installation category in equipment taxonomy. Display label only; original equipmentType key is preserved. Center means center-channel speaker, not a location control.
In-wall speaker: Speaker enclosure/installation category in equipment taxonomy. Display label only; original equipmentType key is preserved. Center means center-channel speaker, not a location control.
Unclassified equipment: Equipment taxonomy has no more specific classification; not an error, missing device, or user permission status.
(original; not SS-CS5M2): Display suffix distinguishing the original Sony SS-CS5 from SS-CS5M2. Preserve model identifier literally; it is not a measured response equivalence.
Cinema speaker: Speaker for cinema sound reproduction, not a film file or video player.
Column speaker: Column-format speaker for sound reinforcement, distinct from the floorstanding home speaker category.
Constant-beamwidth speaker: Constant angular acoustic coverage/beam width across frequency; not constant bandwidth or frequency response. CBT examples verified with official JBL documentation.
Omnidirectional speaker: Speaker radiating in all directions; not a microphone pickup pattern.
Outdoor speaker: Speaker designed for outdoor use; not an output device selector.
Panel speaker: Panel-format speaker category, including planar/electrostatic models; not an application UI panel.
Portable PA speaker: Portable public-address/sound-reinforcement speaker; PA is not a country or personal assistant.
Soundbar: Integrated elongated speaker system commonly used with televisions.
Surround speaker: Speaker used for surround audio channels; not an app surround-mode toggle.
Touring PA speaker: Professional sound-reinforcement speaker for touring/live events, distinct from portable PA.
Unsupported Studio profile schema: Saved Studio setup schema/version or required top-level structure is unsupported. This is a file format, not a visual theme or room calibration profile.
Studio profile has an invalid numeric fi: Saved Studio setup numeric field is wrong type, nonfinite or outside its supported range. JSON numbers use invariant syntax; do not reinterpret them according to the interface locale.
Studio profile has an invalid boolean fi: Saved Studio setup requires a JSON true/false field. Wrong type or missing value is rejected; do not confuse this with an audio level or textual yes/no preference.
Invalid Studio channel count: Session channel count must be 1..256; audio channels, not stations.
Invalid Studio profile channel count: Saved profile channels array must be nonempty and contain at most 256 channels.
Invalid Studio channel name or filters: Saved channel name must be a nonempty string up to 80 characters, and bands must be an array; filter list, not filter-value validation.
Too many Studio channel filters: Per-channel EQ filter count exceeds 64; unchanged processing bound.
Invalid Studio route: Saved audio routing edge must contain exactly three entries: output index, input index, mixing coefficient.
Duplicate Studio route: Same input/output routing edge appears more than once; not duplicated media or road route.
Invalid route indexes or weight: Audio route indices must be whole channel indices in range and mixing coefficient magnitude at most 4; weight means a signed mixing coefficient, not physical mass.
Invalid route number: A saved audio routing entry contains a nonnumeric or nonfinite number.
Too many Studio routes: Saved audio routing edge count exceeds channel-count squared.
Invalid filter type: Filter type numeric identifier must be a whole supported enum value; not a file type.
Shared and channel EQ exceed 64 filters;: Sum of shared EQ and channel EQ must not exceed 64 filters. Remove channel filters, not speaker profiles. Keep the limit 64.
Invalid enhancement parameter count: Enhancement array must contain the required number of parameters.
Invalid enhancement parameter type: Enhancement parameter must be a JSON number; do not reinterpret strings or Boolean values.
Enhancements outside supported ranges: Enhancement values fail the supported range validation; not frequency coverage or wireless range.

Cable setup launch progress. %1 is stable VB-CABLE name. Opening installer, not claim of successful installation.
%1 setup did not finish. Retry using the: Nonzero setup exit progress notice, excluding restart-required code 3010. %1 is driver name (SoundCurrent Audio or VB-CABLE). Uninstall: Windows Start-menu shortcut action removing this application. Distinct from Quit or closing the UI. Driver removal remains optional shared-driver policy.
Invalid audio route: loopback requires a: Owned Windows routing diagnostic displayed at the desktop boundary. Loopback captures a render source; it must not capture the processed destination, which would feed audio back into itself. No change to routing IDs or backend strings. Contextual AI translation only; native review unverified.
Cannot open input WAVE file: Owned offline-render input-file opening failure. WAVE is the file format, not an acoustic wave. Does not assert the cause is missing media or permissions. Preserve WAVE literally. Contextual AI translation; native verification unverified.
Truncated WAVE file: Owned WAVE binary read failure: expected bytes cannot be read completely. Does not mean musical trim/crop or an intentionally shortened clip. WAVE denotes the file format. Contextual AI translation; native verification unverified.
Cannot create output WAVE file: Owned offline WAVE writer file-creation failure, including staging output. Does not assert missing disk space or permission denial. WAVE denotes the file format. Contextual AI translation; native verification unverified.
Cannot seek to WAVE audio: Owned WAVE file-stream seek failure when positioning the read cursor at the audio-data offset. Not device discovery or searching for a song. Preserve WAVE file-format identifier. Contextual AI translation; native verification unverified.
Invalid RIFF size: Owned file-parser validation: declared RIFF extent is too small or exceeds actual file length. Not sample rate or channel count. Preserve RIFF identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Chunk extends beyond RIFF bounds: Owned file-parser validation: a binary chunk payload length extends beyond the declared RIFF extent. Not an audio clip region or buffer overload. Preserve RIFF identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Invalid WAVE read buffer: Owned WaveReader buffer validation: destination sample count is not a multiple of file channel count. Not a playback device buffer or memory allocation failure. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Invalid output WAVE format: Owned WaveWriter output format validation before file creation. Not an input file parsing error. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Could not flush WAVE output: Owned WaveWriter finalization failure: flushing buffered file writes failed. Not clearing effects, deleting audio or changing speaker output. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Could not close WAVE output: Owned WaveWriter finalization failure: closing output file stream reported an error. Not closing the GUI or stopping an audio device. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Could not write WAVE header: Owned WaveWriter failure writing binary format/header metadata to output file. Header is not a UI title. Preserve WAVE identifier. Does not assert a particular disk failure cause. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Could not write WAVE audio: Owned WaveWriter failure writing sample data into an output file. Not speaker playback or microphone recording. Preserve WAVE identifier. Does not assert a particular disk failure cause. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Incomplete WAVE output: Owned WaveWriter finalization validation: written frame count differs from the declared output frame count. Not merely a quiet or short musical passage. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Truncated chunk header: Owned RIFF parser validation: fewer than eight bytes remain for a chunk header. Header means binary metadata, not a UI title. Not an intentionally trimmed audio clip. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Invalid valid-bit count: Owned extensible WAVE metadata check: valid bits per sample must be greater than zero and not exceed stored bits per sample. Not file length, bitrate or successful packet count. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Invalid float WAVE format: Owned extensible WAVE floating-point validation: valid-bit field must be 32 for supported float samples. Float means floating-point numbers, not floating playback position. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Speaker mask does not match channel coun: Owned extensible WAVE metadata validation: nonzero speaker-position bitmask must have one set bit per audio channel. Mask means bitmask, not physical speaker covering or EQ curve. Not a hardware fault. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Invalid output speaker mask: Owned WAVE writer validation of output speaker-position bitmask against output channel count. Metadata error, not disconnected speakers or balance. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Missing RIFF padding byte: Owned RIFF parser validation: the alignment padding byte after an odd-length binary chunk is outside declared extent. Not audio silence, delay or padded samples. Preserve RIFF identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Excessive number of RIFF chunks: Owned RIFF parser resource limit: more than 4096 binary chunks. Chunk means container data block, not track, clip or channel. Preserve RIFF identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Output exceeds the RIFF/WAVE 4 GiB limit: Owned WaveWriter size validation: output payload plus RIFF header must fit supported 32-bit RIFF size. Preserve RIFF/WAVE and 4 GiB literally; GiB is binary size, not GB. Does not mean insufficient RAM or free disk space. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
WAVE output exceeds its declared length: Owned WaveWriter frame-count validation: attempted sample writes exceed the frame count declared for the output. Not exceeding volume, clipping threshold or speaker capability. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Input is too short for RIFF/WAVE: Owned parser minimum byte-length check before reading 12-byte RIFF/WAVE header. Not recording duration or speaker response. Preserve RIFF/WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Truncated extensible WAVE format: Owned WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE header validation: extension structure lacks declared fields or length. Extensible is the format variant, not ability to lengthen music. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Missing or incomplete WAVE audio: Owned WaveReader validation: format/data chunk is missing or data length is not a whole number of frames. Not missing microphone, silent samples or absent speaker sound. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Multiple WAVE data chunks are unsupporte: Owned WaveReader support limitation: a second binary data chunk was encountered. Not multichannel audio, multiple tracks or multiple selected files. Preserve WAVE identifier. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Only little-endian RIFF/WAVE is supporte: Owned WAVE reader format support: RIFF/WAVE little-endian byte order only; big-endian RIFX is not supported. Little-endian is byte ordering, not audio phase or low frequencies. Preserve RIFF/WAVE. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Only PCM16/24/32 or float32 WAVE is supp: Owned WAVE reader supports signed integer PCM 16/24/32-bit or 32-bit floating-point samples. Preserve PCM16/24/32, float32 and WAVE literally; numbers are bits per sample, not sample rates or channel counts. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Invalid WAVE frame alignment or byte rat: Owned WAVE file metadata check: block alignment must equal channel count times bytes per sample, and byte rate must equal sample rate times block alignment. Not latency, visual frame alignment or clock sync. Preserve WAVE. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Unsupported WAVE rate or channel count: Owned WaveReader file-format support limit: channel count must be 1..maxChannels and sample rate 8000..384000 Hz. Rate means sample rate, not bitrate or playback speed. Not live device capability. Preserve WAVE. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Missing, duplicate or oversized WAVE for: Owned WaveReader fmt-chunk validation: no duplicate format chunk and payload size must be 16..4096 bytes. Format means binary metadata, not file extension or project type. Preserve WAVE. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Unsupported extensible WAVE subtype: Owned WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE subtype identifier validation: GUID tail is unsupported. Not a physical speaker model or plugin type. Preserve WAVE. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Missing option value: Owned CLI parser error: an option requiring a following argument has no value. Not an unavailable UI choice or lost saved setting. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Invalid finite numeric argument: Owned CLI from_chars numeric parser rejects invalid syntax, partial parses, NaN and infinity. Finite means mathematically finite, not final. Numeric option remains locale-independent machine syntax. Contextual AI review; native verification unverified.
Wrong number of colon-separated fields: Standalone CLI colon-delimited numeric option has an exact required field count (EQ: 4, filters/routes: 3, gain: 2). Colon syntax remains unchanged; this is not a CSV delimiter preference.
Channel indexes are one-based and must e: Standalone CLI channel numbers start at 1; zero, fractions and numbers beyond the available channel count are rejected. This does not change internal zero-based indexes or routing.
Tail must be between 0 and 30 seconds: Standalone CLI --tail appends this many seconds of zero input after the source to render delay/reverb decay. Inclusive range 0–30 seconds; not animal anatomy, input duration or reverb decay parameter. Audio processing and flag syntax stay invariant.
Unknown option: %1: Standalone CLI diagnostic for an unrecognized command-line flag. %1 is the exact option spelling supplied by the caller; preserve it verbatim and do not translate/reparse it. Not a missing option value or unknown equipment model.
Route gain must be between -120 and +12: Standalone --route OUT:IN:DB matrix entry gain, inclusive -120 to +12 dB; machine numeric syntax and dB identifier unchanged. Not post gain or channel trim, whose ranges differ.
Invalid routing matrix: ChannelRouter rejected the supplied matrix dimensions or finite weight values. Mathematical audio mixing/routing matrix, not a visual grid.
Invalid routing buffer: ChannelRouter rejected interleaved input/output sample spans with incompatible sizes. Internal memory buffer, not physical routing hardware or network buffering.
Invalid processing buffer: AudioEngine reported an invalid interleaved sample buffer size relative to its channel count. Internal memory buffer, not an effect preset or playback device.
Cannot protect output staging directory: POSIX permissions could not be restricted to owner-only on the renderer staging directory. Local temporary files, not encryption or network security. Windows branch does not emit this diagnostic.
Cannot publish output: %1; choose a new: Local atomic no-overwrite hard-link publication failed. %1 is the filesystem error detail and must be preserved verbatim. Publication means moving the completed render into its requested local filename, not Internet sharing. Hard links are filesystem links, not symbolic links.
Rendered %1 -> %2 channels, %3 frames at: Successful standalone offline render. %1 input channels, %2 output channels, %3 audio frame count (not per-channel samples), %4 sample rate. Keep Hz and -> identifiers. Count-label wording is allowed to avoid number-dependent noun inflection.
Peak before clipping: %1; clipped sample: Successful standalone render statistics. %1 linear absolute peak before hard clipping (not dB); %2 individual clipped samples across channels; %3 invalid/nonfinite input or processing samples. Numbers and processing stay unchanged; labels may avoid plural inflection.
SoundCurrent Studio offline renderer (no: Standalone renderer works on files without opening an audio device or live stream. Offline means non-live rendering, not a requirement to disconnect from the Internet. Preserve product name SoundCurrent Studio.
Usage: %1 [options]: CLI usage line. %1 is invariant executable name, required flags and example filenames. Translate only the surrounding usage/options words; flags and filenames remain literal.
Channel indexes start at 1. Existing out: CLI channel numbers are one-based. Existing output file protection is unconditional: the renderer refuses overwriting, including races at publication. No option to overwrite is implied.
interface language; unsupported tags use: CLI --language: selects interface catalog, normalizes tag case/separators and uses supported base language where available. Unresolved tags fall back to English. Does not change audio or numeric argument syntax.
1-256 output channels (default: input co: CLI output channel count is inclusive 1–256, default equal to input WAVE channel count. Preserve the literal numeric range 1-256. Not input device selection.
explicit matrix gain; using any route cl: CLI --route OUT:IN:DB: when any explicit route exists the matrix starts at zero; only specified routes remain. Clearing defaults does not restore identity or automatic routing.
peaking EQ for one output channel; repea: CLI --eq CH:HZ:DB:Q adds one peaking/bell filter to an output channel, repeatable within 64 filters per channel. Not peak detection or a shelf filter. CLI flag and argument tokens remain unchanged.
optional channel low-pass (e.g. LFE): CLI low-pass output-channel filter attenuates high frequencies, passing low frequencies; LFE is only an example channel use, not an automatic speaker role. Preserve LFE identifier.
optional channel high-pass: CLI high-pass output-channel filter attenuates low frequencies, passing high frequencies. Optional means absent unless specified. Not treble boost.
output channel trim, -60 to +24 dB: Per-output-channel gain/trim, inclusive -60 to +24 dB. Preserve signs, bounds and dB; this is not the wider global post-gain range.
overall post gain, -84 to +24 dB: Global post-gain control, inclusive -84 to +24 dB, applied to all channels. Preserve signs, bounds and dB; do not substitute the narrower channel trim range.
1-2000 ms (default 250): Delay duration in milliseconds, inclusive 1–2000, default 250. Preserve numeric CLI syntax and ms.
0-0.9 (default .35): Delay feedback fraction inclusive 0–0.9, default .35. Numeric examples retain decimal dot accepted by from_chars, independent of regional decimal comma.
wet fraction 0-1 (enables delay): Delay wet/processed-signal mix fraction inclusive 0–1; zero dry, one wet. Setting the option marks delay enabled even if zero mix is inaudible. Wet is audio mixing, not humidity.
.1-10 seconds (default 1.5): Reverb decay parameter in seconds inclusive .1–10, default 1.5; used in feedback decay calculation. Numeric examples keep CLI decimal dots.
0-.95 (default .4): Reverb damping coefficient inclusive 0–.95, default .4; larger value damps high-frequency recirculation more. Not damping in dB or delay feedback.
wet fraction 0-1 (enables reverb): Reverb wet/processed-signal mix fraction inclusive 0–1; zero dry, one wet. Setting the option marks reverb enabled. Wet is audio mixing, not humidity.
append 0-30 seconds to render effect tai: Append 0–30 seconds of zero input after source audio so delay/reverb tails can decay into the export. Does not extend input media or change reverb decay itself. Preserve 0-30.
disable automatic EQ headroom: Disable automatic per-channel EQ gain compensation/headroom. Does not disable final clipping or invalid-sample protection.
bypass EQ, effects, gains and mute: Bypass engine EQ, delay/reverb/enhancements, channel/global gain and channel mute. Routing matrix still applies; final clipping and invalid-sample protection still apply. No device-routing bypass is implied.
Input accepts PCM integer 16/24/32 or IEEE float32 in little-endian RIFF/WAVE. Output is float32 WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE. Preserve PCM16/24/32, float32 (twice), RIFF/WAVE and WAVE format identifiers.
